session_cue.text: Drop Dead Ned's killer wasp buzzing in a necklace jar

previous.text: The party reached Brandonsford at sunset, following a treasure map into land they didn't know.
Eric the Reeve offered a bounty on a dragon troubling Brandonsford, the town's first since Sir Brandon's legendary kill.
Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter at the Clumsy Fox, offered to join the party against the dragon for pay.
Sir Phidipaldi dismissed George's black dragon as an illusion and slapped Eric the Reeve with his glove.
Dr. Uriah met the thief Drop Dead Ned, who offered himself and his killer wasp for hire.
Sir Phidipaldi struck a deal with Quinn of the Golden Egg to get back at Bentley over stolen ale.

current.where_you_are: Sir Phidipaldi is in the Golden Egg Tavern with its owner, Quinn. Bentley escorted him over from the Clumsy Fox Tavern across the street.

Your goals.text: Find the treasure on the party's map, which the party assumes lies at one of its marked spots.
Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford, though the party hasn't formally taken the job.
Fight Eric the Reeve in the dawn duel Sir Phidipaldi demanded.

Standing in your way.text: Eric the Reeve hasn't accepted Sir Phidipaldi's challenge, so the dawn duel can't go ahead.

What could help.text: The one-armed woodsman George met the dragon and calls it a black dragon, not a big one. Eric says George lives a couple of houses down from the Clumsy Fox and might come by tonight.

Quinn and Sir Phidipaldi agreed to stage a fake ale shipment at the Golden Egg to see what happens overnight. Quinn brings bottles to fill with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a show of delivering them.
Eric the Reeve offers 1000 gold to whoever kills the dragon and drags its body into Brandonsford.
Lady Hilda could help the party fight the dragon if they pay her.
Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda they would come back for her after talking to the Reeve. She says she couldn't kill the dragon herself.
Drop Dead Ned offers himself and his killer wasp for 100 gold a week, if he gets to kill people with it. He'll rebate 5 gold per kill if he can do what he wants with the victims.
Farmer Gill offers to sell Dunk his shabby mule Shamus for 100 gold.

Still unanswered.text: Who or what really takes Quinn's good stock each night, leaving glasses empty or knocked over? Quinn blames Bentley.
Where are the places marked on the party's treasure map, in land the party doesn't know?
Where is the dragon to be found outside Brandonsford?
What has stopped shipments reaching Brandonsford for months, and what happened to Bentley's restock due a week ago?
Why won't Warwick the smith sell his mithril chain shirt? Gill says it may be the best in the world and fits a normal-sized person.

Promises and debts.text: Sir Phidipaldi must help Quinn get back at Bentley, and Quinn will pay him 100 gold for it.

Meanwhile.text: Farmer Gill's three sons are hunting the dragon now. They may kill it and claim the Reeve's bounty first.
Reginald the Frog warns that a trickster Clurichen comes into town from the riverbanks each night. He says to stay away from wherever it goes.
A black dragon near Brandonsford tore off George's arm and may harm others.

threads.name: The unrecognized treasure map
threads.note: The party is following a treasure map whose marked locations they don't recognize, and the treasure's whereabouts remain unknown.

threads.name: The Clurichen of the riverbanks
threads.note: Reginald warned of a trickster creature that comes into town nightly and should be avoided; this danger stands on its own and is still open.

threads.name: The dragon near Brandonsford
threads.note: A black dragon troubles the town and Eric the Reeve offers 1000 gold for its body; leads (George, Gill's sighting, the Sir Brandon legend) and rivals (Gill's sons) all bear on this one hunt, which is not yet done.

threads.name: Hiring Lady Hilda
threads.note: Lady Hilda offered to join for money against the dragon, and Sir Phidipaldi said they would come back for her after talking to the Reeve (beat_10), so it serves the dragon hunt and is still pending.

threads.name: Bentley's missing shipment
threads.note: Bentley's restock shipment is a week overdue and nothing has reached town in months; no one is known to have gone after it.

threads.name: Sir Phidipaldi's challenge to Eric the Reeve
threads.note: Sir Phidipaldi slapped Eric and challenged him to a dawn duel, which Eric never accepted (beat_19); Bentley banned fighting and ejected Phidipaldi (beat_24), but the quarrel is unsettled.

threads.name: Drop Dead Ned's offer of hire
threads.note: Ned offered himself and his killer wasp for 100 gold a week, and Dr. Uriah said he'd think about it, so the offer stands.

threads.name: Shamus the mule
threads.note: Gill offered to sell Shamus for 100 gold, Dunk asked to trade work instead, and Dunk is still thinking it over.

threads.name: Warwick the smith and his mithril shirt
threads.note: Warwick displays a superb mithril chain shirt he refuses to sell and is growing strangely paranoid, both open matters the party might act on.

threads.name: Quinn's vanishing ale
threads.note: Quinn's stock disappears nightly and he suspects Bentley; Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help for 100 gold and planned a fake shipment, which is still to be carried out.

facts.text: Find the treasure shown on the party's treasure map, which the party assumes lies at one of the map's marked spots.
Where are the locations marked on the party's treasure map? The party doesn't recognize them, and the land around Brandonsford is wholly unknown to them.

Reginald the Frog warns that every night a little trickster creature called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into Brandonsford, up to no good, and that the party should stay away from wherever it goes.
Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford.
facts.uncertain_reason: The party never formally took the job. Sir Phidipaldi said they would talk to the Reeve and return for Lady Hilda, but he also told Eric that black dragons don't exist.

facts.text: Eric the Reeve offers 1000 gold to whoever kills the dragon and drags its body into Brandonsford.

The one-armed woodsman George encountered the dragon and describes it as a black dragon, not a big one. Eric says he lives a couple of houses down from the Clumsy Fox and might come to the tavern tonight.
Lady Hilda's offer to join the dragon hunt for pay could help the party fight the dragon.
A black dragon lurks near Brandonsford. It tore off the woodsman George's arm and may harm others.
Farmer Gill's three sons are out hunting the dragon now, and Gill is sure they will bring it back. They may kill it and claim the Reeve's bounty before the party does.
Where is the dragon to be found outside Brandonsford?
Sir Brandon's dragon was killed and ripped apart centuries ago. Where did this new dragon come from?

Lady Hilda, a seasoned red-headed noblewoman in chain mail and shield at the Clumsy Fox, will join the party against the dragon for pay (fee not yet named), though she says she couldn't kill it herself. Sir Phidipaldi told her they would come back for her services after talking to the Reeve.
What has stopped shipments from reaching Brandonsford for months, and what happened to Bentley's tavern restock shipment that was due a week ago?
Sir Phidipaldi intends to fight Eric the Reeve in the duel at dawn he demanded after slapping him with his glove.
Eric the Reeve has not accepted Sir Phidipaldi's challenge; he only said, flustered, that Sir Phidipaldi was more skilled at adventure. This blocks the dawn duel.
Bentley, owner of the Clumsy Fox, has banned fighting between Sir Phidipaldi and Eric the Reeve and sent Sir Phidipaldi to sleep at the Golden Egg, which constrains pursuing the duel at his tavern.

Drop Dead Ned, a greasy-haired thief at the Clumsy Fox, offers himself and his killer wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, willing to do anything as long as he gets to kill people with the wasp. He offers a 5-gold rebate per kill if he can do what he wants with the victims. Dr. Uriah said he'd think about it; accepting requires paying the fee.
Farmer Gill offers to sell Dunk his shabby mule Shamus for 100 gold.
Dunk asked to trade work for Shamus instead of paying; Farmer Gill says the big work needed is killing the dragon outside town. Gill never said that killing it would pay for the mule.
facts.uncertain_reason: Gill named the work needed but never confirmed that killing the dragon would pay for Shamus.

facts.text: Gill says Warwick the smith displays a superb mithril chain shirt, perhaps the best in the world and sized for a normal-sized person, but always refuses to sell it. Why won't Warwick sell the mithril shirt?

Gill says Warwick is growing more paranoid, adding lucky charms to his shop daily and covering a wall with clovers; Gill guesses they are meant to keep away Ingrid the potion seller, who he says is hot for Warwick. What is Warwick really warding against?
Gill says Ingrid, who runs the alchemist shop in Brandonsford, is where to go for potions; the party could visit her to buy them.
Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help Quinn, owner of the Golden Egg, get back at Bentley, whom Quinn believes steals his ale each night, in exchange for 100 gold.
Quinn offers Sir Phidipaldi 100 gold for helping him get back at Bentley, payable once the help is given.

Plan agreed with Quinn: stage a fake shipment at the Golden Egg. Quinn brings up bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering ale to see what happens overnight.

Quinn says his good stock is gone by morning, with half the glasses empty or knocked over, and blames Bentley because the Clumsy Fox is so popular. Who or what is really taking Quinn's ale each night?
